classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange to reveal a tangent difference, justify dividing by its denominator, and prove that every general candidate violates the original domain.

content.prompt:
Show that the trigonometric equation
$$\tan(3x)-\tan(2x)\tan(3x)-\tan(2x)=1$$
has no solutions for any domain of $x$.

answer.short:
No solutions.

The tangent difference identity gives $x=45^\circ+180^\circ k$, but $\tan(2x)$ is undefined at every candidate.
answer.worked:
Rearrange:
$$\begin{align*}\tan(3x)-\tan(2x)&=1+\tan(2x)\tan(3x).\end{align*}$$
The right-hand side cannot be zero: that would require equal tangent values whose product is $-1$, which is impossible for real values.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\tan(3x)-\tan(2x)}{1+\tan(2x)\tan(3x)}&=1\\\tan(3x-2x)&=1\\\tan x&=1\\x&=45^\circ+180^\circ k,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z\\2x&=90^\circ+360^\circ k.\end{align*}$$
At every candidate, $\tan(2x)$ is undefined. Therefore the original equation has no solutions.
